meta.dataset: Tech-enablement ("OS") value-creation evidence file: ServiceOS (Punctual Pros), GridOS (CET), FirmOS (Frontline), LabOS (Thomas Scientific), SignalOS (BPI), HarborOS (Fair Harbor)
meta.scope_note: Six active BSP portfolio companies. Smith + Howard (exited to TPG, Aug 2026) is excluded. CET guidance: no NYC expansion; GridOS is New England only.
meta.method: Web research on 2026-10-06 (search plus direct fetches of press releases, SEC filings, banker reports and vendor pages), combined with existing verified portal sources (public comparables, Punctual Pros market research, Punctual Pros filings, CET filings, Frontline filings, Thomas Scientific filings, BPI filings, rival filings, Fair Harbor filings). Each valuation evidence item states its number and source; derived arithmetic (e.g., members per technician, implied EV/revenue) is labelled "derived". KPI benchmark baselines and targets come from sourced benchmarks; where a company actual is not public, baseline or target is null. roadmap assumption items are explicit analyst assumptions (labelled est.) tied by evidence links to items in this file; USD EBITDA impact = low/high revenue estimate x low/high margin points.
caveats: Reported deal multiples (Champions 18.5x, Sila ~17x) are press estimates from people familiar with the deals; sponsors did not disclose terms.
Multiples for scaled roll-ups mostly reflect scale, density and M&A runway, not technology alone. This file credits only a fraction of the typical-to-premium spread to tech enablement.
Vendor case studies (ServiceTitan Pricebook Pro, Rilla, Avoca, True Fit, Bold Metrics, Rewst) are self-reported, self-selected and unaudited; treat them as upper bounds.
Portfolio company revenue/EBITDA figures are low-confidence analyst estimates from the portal filings sources, not company disclosures.
Vendor pricing marked third-party comes from pricing-guide sites and may be stale; confirm with vendors before budgeting.
MetricNet first-level-resolution and cost-per-ticket figures date from 2011 and are directional only.
The ServiceTitan TitanAdvisor quartile figure (20% vs 8%) was taken from S-1 search extraction; the direct fetch confirmed other S-1 figures but not this one.
Thomas Scientific's capital structure (est. 7-10x leverage, Dec-2027 maturity) dominates its exit value; LabOS multiple expansion is secondary to EBITDA and refinancing.
meta.thesis_summary: BSP's six active companies are services businesses whose exit multiples depend on how predictable, recurring and scalable their earnings look to the next buyer. Banker data show this directly: PKF puts project-heavy, low-retention HVAC firms at 5-6x EBITDA and repeatable-service firms with value-enhancing in-house capabilities at 10x+, and Capstone/IMAP expect a 3.0-turn spread between typical (6.8x) and premium (9.8x) middle-market deals. Each "OS" is a named, buyer-legible operating system assembled mostly from proven vendors (ServiceTitan, Procore, ConnectWise/Kaseya, Shopify Plus/Coupa, Brandwatch/Zignal, Shopify/Klaviyo) plus a thin BSP data layer from the portal, not custom software. ServiceOS for Punctual Pros is the lead case: HVAC call booking rates average 38% versus 59% at 25+ technician shops, pricebook adopters grew tickets 14% vs 8%, and scaled membership-dense companies (Champions ~18.5x, Sila ~17x) are where the premium sits. GridOS (CET) and FirmOS (Frontline) turn project and ticket work into measured, recurring service lines (solar/SCADA O&M, security and e-billing revenue cycle), the attributes PKF and Aventis say buyers pay for. LabOS (Thomas Scientific) is an EBITDA and cost-to-serve program benchmarked to Avantor's ~80% digital transactions and Grainger's ~15.6% digital growth vs ~2% rep-led growth, because leverage, not multiple, drives that exit. SignalOS (BPI) and HarborOS (Fair Harbor) productize monitoring and retention, following Stagwell's Marketing Cloud (+230%) and DTC retention economics (5 points of retention lifting profit 25-95%, per Bain). Across the six, analyst assumptions total roughly $6.0-12.4M of investment for 0.5-5 points of EBITDA margin and 0.5-2.5 turns of EBITDA multiple (0.2-0.5x revenue for Fair Harbor), each tied to sourced evidence and labelled est.

multiple_premium_summary.headline: Up to ~3 turns of EBITDA is the quality premium the evidence supports for recurring, visible, tech-enabled services earnings. Tech enablement can claim about 0.5-2.5 turns of it, depending on the company; 17-20x roll-up prints come from scale.

pp.support: PKF 5-6x vs 10x+ grid; Capstone 6.8x vs 9.8x; Champions ~18.5x and Sila ~17x at scale; ServiceTitan heavy users grow GTV 20% vs 8%.
pp.strength: strong for direction, medium for size

cet.support: PKF grid (service mix, retention, in-house capabilities); Capstone spread; electrical M&A slowed to 99 deals in 2025 (buyers more selective); Procore 95% GRR.

fl.support: Aventis MSP size curve 5.2x to 11.2x and churn/recurring drivers; entry already ~12-15x (est.); Kaseya security-driven margins; Clio legal-software valuation.

ts.support: Avantor ~80% digital transactions and Grainger digital growth support EBITDA/growth, not a disclosed multiple premium; capital structure dominates.
ts.strength: weak for multiple, medium for EBITDA

bpi.support: PPHC ~8.4x floor vs 10-13x estimated sponsor exit; FGS $1.7B EV; Stagwell Marketing Cloud +230%; Publicis +5.6% organic vs WPP decline.

fh.support: Retention economics (Bain/HBR), returns (NRF 19.3% online), margin dispersion among DTC comps (LULU 24.4% vs 3-6%).

multiple_premium_summary.what_it_does_not_support: No source isolates a pure "technology premium" with a control group; the premiums observed bundle scale, recurring mix, margin and growth. Use the ranges as analyst assumptions in the techos calculator, not as market facts.

meta.public_comps_tie_in: See data/research/public_comps.json sector benchmarks: residential home services median EBITDA margin 15.1% (Frontdoor 24.2% on a membership model); commercial electrical median 11.2%; legal/BPO managed services 16.9%; communications agencies and apparel DTC are bimodal (Publicis/LULU vs WPP/smaller DTC).

items.title: Blackstone buys Champions Group at ~18.5x trailing EBITDA
items.claim: Blackstone (BXPE) agreed to buy residential HVAC/plumbing/electrical company Champions Group from Odyssey for about $2.5B, reported at about 18.5x trailing EBITDA; Champions runs 1,800+ technicians and ~150,000 active members.
items.note: Multiple is a press estimate; Blackstone did not disclose terms. Scaled, membership-dense company; not directly comparable to a ~$22M franchisee.

items.title: Goldman Sachs Alternatives buys Sila Services at ~17x EBITDA
items.claim: Goldman Sachs Alternatives agreed to buy Sila Services (30+ HVAC/plumbing/electrical brands in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic) from Morgan Stanley Capital Partners for about $1.7B, ~17x LTM EBITDA of just under $100M including pending acquisitions (~20x excluding them).
items.metric_unit: x EV / LTM EBITDA (reported, incl. pending acquisitions)
items.source_name: HomePros (citing people familiar); Goldman Sachs AM press release (terms not disclosed)
items.note: Sila is a Mid-Atlantic/Northeast peer and an Avoca customer (ve-09).

items.title: Apex Service Partners minority stake at ~$10B valuation
items.claim: Apollo agreed to buy a minority stake in Alpine-backed Apex Service Partners at about $10B including debt; Apex reports 75 local brands in 46 states, 13,000+ employees and over $3B of revenue (implying roughly 3.3x revenue, analyst arithmetic).
items.note: EV/revenue of ~3.3x is derived ($10B / >$3B) and is an upper bound because revenue is stated as "over $3B". EBITDA not disclosed. Also in data/research/pp_market.json.

items.title: Wrench Group recap explicitly funds "digital transformation"
items.claim: TSG Consumer Partners and Oak Hill took a significant minority stake in Leonard Green-controlled Wrench Group (5,800+ staff, 1.75M+ customers a year, 24 markets) with the stated aim to "advance Wrench Group's digital transformation and disciplined M&A strategy"; terms were not disclosed.
items.note: Shows that upmarket sponsors underwrite home-services companies partly on digital capability; no number to cite.

items.title: PKF: 10x+ EBITDA for repeatable-service, high-visibility HVAC businesses vs 5-6x for project-heavy
items.claim: PKF Investment Banking's Summer 2026 HVAC M&A update says services transaction multiples stayed "north of 10x EBITDA" for high-revenue-visibility, high-margin businesses with a large service component, and its valuation-attribute grid places undifferentiated, project-heavy, low-retention firms at 5.0-6.0x versus 10.0x+ for value-enhancing in-house capabilities, high retention and repeatable service.
items.metric_unit: x EBITDA (lower bound of premium band; discount band 5.0-6.0x)
items.source_name: PKF O'Connor Davies / PKF Investment Banking, U.S. HVAC M&A Industry Update Summer 2026
items.note: Grid rows include "In-House Capabilities and Innovation", "Customer Retention", "Business Mix (Project vs. Services)" and "Earnings Visibility"; tech-enablement moves several rows at once.

items.title: Capstone/IMAP: premium deals price ~3 turns above typical
items.claim: Capstone Partners and IMAP's 2025-2026 survey expects average typical and premium middle-market M&A EBITDA multiples of 6.8x and 9.8x in 2026, a 3.0-turn spread between typical and premium-quality assets.
items.metric_unit: x EBITDA spread (9.8x premium minus 6.8x typical)
items.source_name: Capstone Partners / IMAP Trends in Global M&A Survey (press release)
items.note: Survey of advisors, not closed-deal data. The 3.0x spread caps how much "quality" re-rating any one lever (including tech) can plausibly claim.

items.title: ServiceTitan FY2026: $82.1B GTV (+20%), NDR >110%, ~10,800 customers
items.claim: ServiceTitan reported FY2026 (Jan-2026 year-end) revenue of $961.0M (+24%), platform revenue of $925.4M (+25%), gross transaction volume of $82.1B (+20%), net dollar retention above 110%, gross dollar retention above 95% and about 10,800 active customers.
items.source_name: ServiceTitan FY2026 results release; Form 10-K FY2026
items.note: Shows contractors keep expanding spend on the operating system; GTV growth (20%) is the volume running through contractors on the software.

items.title: ServiceTitan S-1: heavy platform users grew GTV 20% vs 8% for light users
items.claim: ServiceTitan's S-1 discloses that from Q1-2021 to Q2-2024 customers in the top quartile of TitanAdvisor (platform-utilization) scores had median year-over-year GTV growth of 20%, versus 8% for the bottom quartile.
items.metric_unit: percentage-point median GTV growth gap (20% vs 8%)
items.note: Correlation, not causation: better operators may both use the software more and grow faster. Our fetch of the S-1 confirmed active-customer, GTV and retention figures; the quartile figure is from the S-1 per search extraction and should be re-checked before external use.

items.title: Avoca (AI CSR for home services) valued at $1B
items.claim: Avoca, an AI call-answering and booking platform for home services, raised $125M+ across Seed/A/B at a $1B valuation, surpassed eight-figure ARR in 2025 and counts TurnPoint Services, Sila and Goettl among customers.
items.note: Capital markets are paying software multiples for the front-office layer of home services; PP can rent this capability rather than build it.

items.title: Pricebook Pro users grew revenue 12% vs 2% for non-users
items.claim: ServiceTitan data on 179 Pricebook Pro adopters showed 2020 revenue up 12% versus 2% for non-users and average ticket growth of 14% versus 8%.
items.note: Vendor-published, COVID-period, self-selected sample.

items.title: Membership-model comp: Frontdoor earns 24.2% EBITDA margin vs 15.1% residential median
items.claim: Frontdoor (home-service plans, a subscription/membership model) posted FY2025 revenue of $2.09B (+13.6%) at an approximate EBITDA margin of 24.2%, versus a 15.1% median for the five residential home-services public comps in the portal data.
items.note: EBITDA = operating income proxy + D&A, unadjusted. Frontdoor is asset-light (subcontracted), so margin is an upper bound for a technician-employing operator.

items.title: Procore: 95% gross / 106% net revenue retention in construction software
items.claim: Procore reported FY2025 revenue of $1,323M (+15%), 17,850 organic customers, 2,710 customers above $100K ARR (+16%), 95% gross revenue retention and 106% net revenue retention.
items.note: Contractors that adopt project-management software rarely leave it; supports a durable digital operating layer at CET.

items.title: Electrical contractor M&A: 99 deals in 2025 vs 140 in 2024, financial buyers ~2/3
items.claim: Cascade Partners counts 99 electrical-contractor acquisitions in 2025 versus 140 in 2024 (-29%), with financial buyers making roughly two-thirds of acquisitions since 2020 and favoring growth-market exposure, diversified revenue and strong management.
items.source_name: EC&M, citing Cascade Partners Electrical Contracting & Utility Infrastructure M&A Update H2 2025
items.note: Fewer deals means buyers are more selective; differentiation (service mix, systems, data) matters more for CET's exit.

items.title: MSP multiples rise with scale: 5.2x (<$5M deals) to 11.2x ($500M+)
items.claim: Aventis Advisors' analysis of 120 private MSP transactions (median deal $38.5M) finds a median ~8.9x EV/EBITDA, rising from 5.2x for deals under $5M to 9.9x for $50-100M, 10.0x for $100-500M and 11.2x above $500M; public MSP comps traded at an 11.4x median in H2 2024 (peak 17.5x in H1 2021).
items.note: Aventis lists drivers as scale, growth, recurring mix (<50% recurring creates hesitation), concentration, churn (>10% a year raises concerns) and AI-driven automation margins.

items.title: Frontline entry estimated at 12-15x adjusted EBITDA
items.claim: Portal research triangulates Frontline's BSP entry at about $230-260M of transaction value on $16-20M adjusted EBITDA, roughly 12-15x, a premium consistent with vertical-specialist, high-recurring MSPs.
items.note: Analyst estimate from disclosed equity and debt; the premium is already in the entry price, so FirmOS must defend rather than create it.

items.title: Clio: legal software at $5B on $500M+ ARR
items.claim: Clio closed a $500M Series G at a $5B post-money valuation alongside its $1B vLex acquisition, after surpassing $500M ARR, about 10x ARR (analyst arithmetic).
items.note: Pure software; shows the value pool around law-firm workflow. Frontline is a services business and should not be valued like Clio; the point is that productized, recurring legal-ops capability is what buyers pay up for.

items.title: Kaseya 2025: security is the top revenue driver for high-margin MSPs
items.claim: Kaseya's 2025 Global MSP Benchmark Report finds 67% of MSPs name security among their five fastest-growing revenue lines, MSPs with 15%+ net margins rank cybersecurity in their top three revenue streams, and 95% say connecting RMM, PSA and documentation is essential to scale.
items.metric_unit: % of MSPs citing security as a top-5 fastest-growing revenue line
items.note: Vendor survey.

items.title: Avantor: ~80% of transactions through digital channels
items.claim: Avantor's FY2025 10-K states that approximately 80% of its transactions came from digital channels, across 300,000+ customer locations.
items.note: Closest public lab-distribution comp for Thomas Scientific; sets the digital-penetration bar. Avantor FY2025 revenue fell 3.4% (public comparables), so digital share is table stakes, not a growth guarantee.

items.title: Grainger: digital Endless Assortment grew ~15.6% vs ~2% for High-Touch in 2025
items.claim: Grainger's FY2025 sales were $17.9B (+4.5%); its digital Endless Assortment segment (Zoro, MonotaRO) grew about 15.6% on a daily organic constant-currency basis while the branch/sales-rep High-Touch segment grew just over 2%, and eProcurement is now close to 40% of its connected ordering channels.
items.metric_unit: % daily organic constant-currency growth, Endless Assortment FY2025
items.source_name: Grainger Q4/FY2025 results release; Distribution Strategy; Digital Commerce 360
items.note: MRO, not lab, but the clearest public evidence that digital distribution channels outgrow rep-led channels in a weak market.

items.title: Stagwell "The Marketing Cloud" grew net revenue 230% in FY2025
items.claim: Stagwell reported FY2025 net revenue of $2,428M (+6%) and adjusted EBITDA of $422M (17% margin on net revenue), with its productized software/data unit The Marketing Cloud delivering 230% year-over-year net revenue growth.
items.metric_unit: % YoY net revenue growth, The Marketing Cloud (FY2025)
items.note: Growth includes acquisitions; Stagwell's own release does not separate organic growth for the unit.

items.title: Publicis (data/tech-led) grew 5.6% organically in 2025 while WPP shrank
items.claim: Publicis Groupe reported 2025 net revenue of EUR 14.547B, +5.6% organic, with an 18.2% operating margin, crediting Epsilon-powered connected media and AI products; WPP's FY2025 revenue fell 8.1% in the portal's public-comps data.
items.note: The holding companies that productized data and tech are the ones still growing.

items.title: PPHC public-affairs comp at ~8.4x; a scaled BPI sponsor exit likely 10-13x
items.claim: Portal research puts PPHC (closest listed DC public-affairs peer) at about 8.4x EV / 2025 adjusted EBITDA at its Jan-2026 IPO price, with 24-26% adjusted EBITDA margins, and estimates a sponsor exit for a scaled, growing BPI at 10-13x.
items.metric_unit: x EV / 2025 adj. EBITDA (PPHC at IPO price)
items.note: The 10-13x sponsor-exit range is an analyst estimate; 8.4x is computed from filed share count, IPO price and net debt.

items.title: KKR values FGS Global at $1.7B EV
items.claim: WPP sold its ~50% stake in strategic-communications firm FGS Global to KKR at a $1.7B enterprise value, described as an attractive multiple of 2023 EBITDA (multiple not disclosed).
items.note: Premium strategic-comms valuations exist at scale; the multiple is not disclosed.

items.title: Retention economics: +5 pts retention lifts profit 25-95%
items.claim: Bain & Company research by Frederick Reichheld, cited in Harvard Business Review, found that increasing customer retention rates by 5% increases profits by 25% to 95%.
items.source_name: Harvard Business Review (Amy Gallo), citing Bain & Company
items.note: Old, cross-industry heuristic; useful for direction, not for sizing.

items.title: DTC apparel margins are bimodal: LULU 24.4% EBITDA vs 2.7-6.4% for smaller peers
items.claim: In the portal's apparel/DTC comps, lululemon earned an approximate 24.4% EBITDA margin in FY2025 while Revolve (6.4%), Crocs (5.7%, impairment-hit) and Duluth (2.7%) earned far less, and Allbirds was negative.
items.note: Brand strength and repeat purchasing, not size alone, separate DTC winners; HarborOS targets the repeat and returns levers.

items.title: Online apparel returns: 19.3% of online sales returned in 2025
items.claim: NRF and Happy Returns estimate that 15.8% of 2025 retail sales ($849.9B) and 19.3% of online sales will be returned.
items.source_name: NRF / Happy Returns 2025 Retail Returns Landscape
items.note: All categories; apparel online return rates are typically higher than the all-category figure, but no apparel-specific figure was verified here.

items.vendor: ServiceTitan (or Housecall Pro for smaller units)
items.category: Field-service management / CRM system of record
items.what_it_does: Call booking, dispatch board, pricebook, memberships, invoicing and payments; the data spine every other ServiceOS module reads from.
items.pricing_note: ServiceTitan: quote-based subscription plus usage fees (payments, financing); not published. Housecall Pro: Basic $49, Essentials $129 per month billed annually, MAX custom, extra users $35/user/month (third-party pricing guide, 2026-02).
items.note: Confirm which FSM PP runs today; Punctual Pros filings lists ServiceTitan data as a data gap.

items.what_it_does: Answers and books inbound calls 24/7 straight into ServiceTitan, quotes configured member/non-member and after-hours fees, and scores human CSR calls (Coach).
items.pricing_note: Not published; third-party estimates of about $1,000-3,500 per month scaled by call volume (unverified).
items.note: Vendor claims include booking rate rising from 55% to 90% at one location (vendor site, unaudited).

items.what_it_does: Records and analyzes in-home sales conversations so managers can coach every comfort advisor and technician without riding along.
items.pricing_note: Not published (quote-based).
items.note: Total Comfort (a TurnPoint company) reports a 9% team-wide close-rate increase (vendor case study).

items.what_it_does: Digital flat-rate pricebook and mobile sales tool for HVAC, plumbing and electrical, with good/better/best options at the kitchen table.
items.pricing_note: SmartPrice Starter $35, Plus $45, Pro $55 per technician per month (Capterra listing); integrated data-license options.

items.what_it_does: Review generation, two-way SMS inbox and text-to-pay for local service brands.
items.pricing_note: Core $399/month, Pro $599/month billed annually; Signature quote-based (third-party pricing guide).

items.what_it_does: Forecast and historical weather feeds that drive the ServiceOS capacity index (heat-wave and cold-snap demand multipliers from Punctual Pros demand model).
items.pricing_note: Tiered API plans (Free, Standard, Plus, Business, Enterprise) by request volume; check current list price on vendor page.
items.note: The portal already uses free NWS/Open-Meteo feeds (Live.forecast), so Weatherbit is optional.

items.what_it_does: Drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs and change orders shared between field, office, GC and owner.
items.pricing_note: Annual fee per product based on Annual Construction Volume (ACV), unlimited users; quote-based (third-party estimate $15-30K/yr for $10-50M ACV).

items.what_it_does: Cloud estimating, graphical takeoff, change management and integrated supplier pricing for electrical/MEP contractors; feeds the GridOS bid board.
items.pricing_note: Subscription, quote-based (pricing requires a consultation).

items.what_it_does: Monitoring, SCADA, analytics and alerting for PV and storage fleets, so NuWave can sell O&M contracts with uptime guarantees.
items.pricing_note: Custom multi-year SaaS contracts (often 5-20 years) by portfolio size and modules; no public per-kW price.
items.note: Stem acquired AlsoEnergy for $695M (Feb 2022).

items.category: SCADA / HMI for pump stations and wastewater
items.what_it_does: Server-licensed SCADA platform with unlimited tags, clients and connections; lets Horton offer remote monitoring of municipal pump stations as a recurring service.
items.pricing_note: Perpetual server license with unlimited tags/clients (modular pricing on vendor site); Cloud Edition is usage-billed.

items.what_it_does: Hardware-agnostic OCPP software to operate, bill and monitor commercial EV chargers CET installs.
items.pricing_note: Per-port subscription; a third-party listing shows about $25/port/month for Level 2 and $50 for DCFC (unverified).
items.note: Alternative: AmpUp.

items.what_it_does: Ticketing, SLAs, contracts and billing (PSA) plus remote monitoring, patching, EDR and backup (RMM).
items.pricing_note: ConnectWise PSA quote-based (reported ~$25-110 per user/month depending on modules). Kaseya 365 Endpoint launched at $3.99 per endpoint/month ($1.75 Express without MDR).

items.what_it_does: No/low-code workflow automation across PSA, RMM and Microsoft 365: onboarding/offboarding, billing reconciliation, ticket triage.
items.pricing_note: Not published (quote-based).
items.note: Rewst reports 1,100+ MSPs automated 6.3B tasks and saved 3.75M hours in H1 2025 (vendor claim).

items.what_it_does: Continuous control monitoring and evidence collection for SOC 2 / ISO 27001; lets Frontline sell outside-counsel-guideline and client security audits as a managed service.
items.pricing_note: Vanta SOC 2 from ~$7,200/yr (1-20 employees); Drata from ~$6,500/yr (reseller pricing, 2026).

items.what_it_does: Formats and submits LEDES invoices to client e-billing portals, checks guideline compliance and tracks rejections/appeals.
items.pricing_note: Not published (quote-based).

items.what_it_does: Customer-specific catalogs and contract pricing, quick reorder, account hierarchies; commercetools for headless/composable builds.
items.pricing_note: Shopify Plus from $2,300/month (3-year term) or $2,500/month (1-year); commercetools quote-based.

items.what_it_does: Punchout catalogs and PO/invoice flow into customers' procurement systems so university and biopharma buyers order inside their own tools.
items.pricing_note: Supplier-side connectivity terms vary by buyer and network; not published.
items.note: Evidence for the channel: ePro is close to 40% of Grainger's connected ordering. Also evaluate Jaggaer/SciQuest for academic buyers.

items.what_it_does: Demand forecasting, replenishment and excess-stock alerts layered on the ERP.
items.pricing_note: From about $400-900/month per third-party listings; annual subscription, quote-based.

items.what_it_does: Typo-tolerant, synonym-aware catalog search (CAS numbers, part numbers, specs) with AI ranking.
items.pricing_note: Grow plan: 10,000 searches/month free, then $0.50 per 1,000 requests (Grow Plus $1.75 per 1,000).

items.what_it_does: Real-time social and web listening, topic clustering and analytics feeding client dashboards and alerts.
items.pricing_note: From roughly $800/month to $3,000+/month, 12-month contracts, implementation $5-20K (third-party estimate).

items.what_it_does: Detects and clusters emerging narratives and threats across news, social and video; used by government and public-affairs teams.
items.pricing_note: Capterra lists a starting price of $49,500/year (usage-based).

items.category: Generative AI content with brand voice
items.what_it_does: Drafts statements, briefs and social copy in each client's brand voice with knowledge assets and approval workflows.
items.pricing_note: Pro $59/seat/month annual ($69 monthly); Business custom (third-party pricing guides).

items.what_it_does: Earned-media monitoring, journalist database and reporting for press and public-affairs teams; the news layer under SignalOS.
items.pricing_note: Private pricing; Vendr-reported median buyer ~$25K/yr, Essentials from ~$7K/yr, add-ons (social listening, contacts) extra (third-party estimates).

items.what_it_does: Storefront, checkout, subscriptions and B2B wholesale channel on one catalog.
items.pricing_note: Shopify Plus from $2,300/month (3-year term) or $2,500/month (1-year).
items.note: Confirm Fair Harbor's current Shopify plan tier.

items.what_it_does: Segmentation, flows (post-purchase, replenishment, win-back) and SMS on unified customer profiles.
items.pricing_note: Priced by active profiles: Email plan about $150/month at 10,000 profiles; Email + SMS about $165/month (third-party pricing guide).

items.what_it_does: Predicts the right size from shopper data to cut fit-related returns and size bracketing.
items.pricing_note: Not published (enterprise SaaS).
items.note: True Fit claims up to 40% fewer fit-related returns; Bold Metrics claims a 17% average reduction in fit-related returns (vendor claims).

items.what_it_does: Digital line sheets and order portal for Nordstrom/specialty doors; reorders and pre-books.
items.pricing_note: Quote-based; third-party listing shows a starting price of about $7,000.

items.what_it_does: Forecasts SKU-level demand by size/color and builds purchase orders; critical for a seasonal swim line.
items.pricing_note: Essentials $119.99/month; higher tiers quote-based by GMV and SKU count (Shopify app listing / third-party guides).

items.baseline_basis: ServiceTitan data, June 2022: HVAC 38%, all trades 42%, shops with fewer than 5 techs 24%.
items.target_basis: ServiceTitan data: shops with 25+ techs booked 59% (same period). Target = large-shop benchmark.
items.lever: Avoca AI CSR + call scoring + ServiceTitan booking scripts

items.baseline_basis: Non-users of a digital flat-rate pricebook: 8% (ServiceTitan, 2020, n=179 adopters vs non-users).
items.target_basis: Pricebook Pro adopters: 14% (same study). Vendor data, low confidence.
items.lever: Profit Rhino / ServiceTitan pricebook with good-better-best

items.baseline_basis: PP membership count not disclosed (data gap; pull from ServiceTitan).
items.target_basis: Champions Group: ~150,000 active members / 1,800+ technicians = ~83 (derived from reported figures; an upper bound because technicians are stated as "more than 1,800").
items.lever: Membership attach at every call + renewal automation (Podium/Klaviyo-style flows)

items.baseline_basis: Pre-coaching baseline = PP's current close rate (not disclosed).
items.target_basis: Rilla case study: Total Comfort (TurnPoint) +9% team-wide close rate; one consultant 23% to 42% in four months (vendor case study).
items.lever: Rilla AI ride-along coaching

items.kpi: Bid win rate on public hard-bid work
items.baseline_basis: ConstructConnect (citing George Hedley/ENR guidance): hard-bid public work wins 10-20%; baseline shown as the range midpoint.

items.revenue_source: data/research/pp_filings.json financial picture (FY2025 pro forma ~$22M, range $16-28M, low-medium confidence)
items.rationale: Booking rate is the biggest lever: ServiceTitan shows HVAC at 38% vs 59% for 25+ tech shops, and pricebook adopters grew ticket 14% vs 8%; a 2-4 point margin gain on ~$22M (est.) is ~$0.3-1.1M. Software run-rate (FSM, Avoca, Rilla, Profit Rhino at $35-55/tech/month, Podium $399-599/month) plus implementation fits a $0.4-0.9M budget. The multiple case leans on PKF (5-6x project-heavy vs 10x+ repeatable service with value-enhancing capabilities) and Capstone (6.8x typical vs 9.8x premium); the 17-18.5x Champions/Sila prints are scale-driven, so only 1.0-2.5 turns are credited to tech enablement at PP's size. Franchise royalties (~7.2-7.5% of revenue) cap the margin upside.
items.label: est. — analyst assumption, not a forecast or company guidance

items.revenue_source: data/research/cet_filings.json estimate table (CET $35-55M + Horton $25-40M + NuWave $2-10M, low confidence)
items.current_ebitda_estimate: CET standalone $3-6M at entry (low confidence); Horton/NuWave not estimated
items.rationale: Combined CET + Horton + NuWave revenue is estimated at ~$62-105M (sum of low-confidence filings estimates). Margin comes from bid selectivity (hard-bid 10-20% win rates vs 30-50% negotiated), less non-productive field time (FMI: 35%), and recurring O&M/SCADA monitoring revenue at NuWave and Horton. Multiple expansion is modest because electrical contracting trades on backlog and mix: PKF's grid rewards repeatable service, retention and in-house capabilities, and Capstone's 3.0-turn typical-to-premium spread is the ceiling; we credit 0.5-1.5 turns. Procore's 95% GRR / 106% NRR shows contractors stick with digital PM once adopted.
items.label: est. — analyst assumption, not a forecast or company guidance

items.revenue_source: data/research/frontline_filings.json estimate table (2025 run-rate $100-140M, low confidence)
items.rationale: Frontline (est. $100-140M revenue, $16-20M EBITDA at close) already entered at an estimated 12-15x, so FirmOS defends the premium rather than creating one. Margin comes from shifting tickets to Level 1/automation (MetricNet $22 vs $62 per ticket; Rewst automation) and from revenue-cycle services that cut e-billing rejections (18% vs 11%) and days-to-pay (62 to 50). Aventis shows MSP multiples rise with scale (9.9-11.2x) and fall with churn above 10%; security attach (Kaseya: top revenue line for 15%+ margin MSPs) and a productized compliance offering (Vanta/Drata) support 0.5-1.5 turns.
items.label: est. — analyst assumption, not a forecast or company guidance

items.revenue_source: data/research/thomas_filings.json estimate table (current revenue $250-320M, low confidence)
items.rationale: Thomas Scientific carries est. 7-10x leverage (est. revenue $250-320M, EBITDA $25-35M) and a December 2027 maturity, so LabOS is an EBITDA and cash program first: digital ordering lowers cost-to-serve and wins long-tail share (Grainger digital +15.6% vs rep-led ~2%; Avantor ~80% digital transactions). Each 0.5 pt of margin on ~$250-320M is ~$1.3-1.6M. Multiple expansion is capped at 0.5-1.0 turns because lab distributors trade on scale and the capital structure dominates exit value; the December 2027 loan maturity sets the timeline.
items.label: est. — analyst assumption, not a forecast or company guidance

items.revenue_source: data/research/bpi_filings.json estimate table (FY2025 net revenue $85-125M, low confidence)
items.rationale: BPI (est. net revenue $85-125M, adj. EBITDA 18-24%) can package narrative monitoring and dashboards as always-on subscriptions, smoothing the election-cycle swing. Evidence: Stagwell's productized Marketing Cloud grew 230%; data/tech-led Publicis grew 5.6% organically while WPP shrank; PPHC trades at ~8.4x with a 24.3% margin. A sponsor exit for a scaled BPI is estimated at 10-13x, so 0.5-2.0 turns of the gap are credited to a productized recurring layer, conditional on showing subscription revenue in the numbers.
items.label: est. — analyst assumption, not a forecast or company guidance

items.rationale: Fair Harbor (est. 2025 revenue $20-35M, EBITDA 0-12%) is margin-starved, so the levers are returns (19.3% online return rate; fit tools report 9.8-40% fewer fit-related returns), repeat purchase (20-30% benchmark) and inventory planning for a seasonal line. 2-5 points of margin is ~$0.4-1.75M. Entry was an estimated 1.3-2.5x revenue; credit is limited to 0.2-0.5x revenue because DTC multiples track growth and margin (LULU 24.4% vs smaller peers at 3-6%), and these levers move margin first.
